sources.claim: OpenAlex works API: metered. Observed 2026-09-11: each search costs $0.001 / 10 credits, daily allowance 1000 credits and $0.10 (reset ~22h); bursts of ~0.3s trigger HTTP 429 and need >=2s pacing plus Retry-After. Keyword search is NOT a field filter (3.28M hits for 'world model'); references are largely absent for arXiv preprints (only 1/8 resolved seeds had any). 2026-10-04: filter title.search requires every word in the title; filter title_and_abstract.search matches title and abstract; combining it with the search parameter ranks the matches by relevance; search alone is full-text relevance. A Chinese phrase finds Chinese-language works (mostly older journal articles), an English-titled arXiv-only query finds almost nothing. With a free key the allowance is 10000 credits / $1 per day.
sources.verification: Live read-only probe tools/data_probe.py: 8/10 seeds resolved to DOI/OpenAlex IDs, abstracts present, citations sparse, future-dated records found without a date ceiling; raw snapshots kept in .local/, report in docs/evidence/2026-09-11-data01-openalex-report.md Live diagnostic 2026-10-04 with counts per query form: docs/evidence/2026-10-04-openalex-discovery-checks.txt.

sources.claim: A work has open_access {is_oa, oa_status (diamond|gold|green|hybrid|bronze|closed), oa_url, any_repository_has_fulltext}, best_oa_location (null when no open copy) and locations[]. A location object has is_oa, landing_page_url, pdf_url (null when only a landing page is known), license (short code such as cc-by, null if unknown), version (publishedVersion|acceptedVersion|submittedVersion) and source. These are candidate links, not proof that automated download is permitted.
sources.verification: Official OpenAlex help pages (work object and locations) fetched 2026-10-04: field names match app/sources.py oa_of(). sources.claim: A free OpenAlex API key (account sign-up, copied from API settings) is sent as the api_key query parameter or as an Authorization bearer token; the two behave the same. The page says a free key raises the daily budget about 10x over keyless use but gives no numbers; requests are metered in credits against a budget that resets at midnight UTC; exceeding it or 100 requests per second gives HTTP 429. The deprecations page (help.openalex.org/api/deprecations) says the polite pool was replaced by API keys before/around February 2026 and that the mailto parameter is ignored.
sources.verification: Official authentication help page fetched 2026-10-04. Measured live 2026-10-04 with the owner's free key: the Authorization bearer header is recognised (a wrong key gives HTTP 401, the real key gives HTTP 200); allowance without a key 1000 credits / $0.10 per day, with the key 10000 credits / $1 per day; each search cost $0.001. mailto: measured the same query with and without a key and with and without mailto; limit, credits used and latency were identical across mailto values, matching the deprecations page. The app therefore no longer sends a user email.

sources.claim: arxiv.org/robots.txt, generic user-agent group: /pdf is explicitly allowed, Crawl-delay is 15 seconds, /e-print, /src, /api and /search are disallowed; the file header says indiscriminate automated downloads are not permitted.
